core_obligations: Parts (1) and (2) (proof lines 857-866): the map A -> A_w is ind-Zariski by construction, and for every finite subset E the morphism Z_E -> X is a bijection, hence so is Z -> X; since Z is contained in X_w the map X_w -> X is surjective, and A -> A_w is faithfully flat by the cited algebra lemma.

Part (3), first half (proof lines 868-882): if y in X_w is not in Z, choose E such that the image of y in X_E is outside Z_E; the reduced closures T_{E'} of the images form an inverse system whose limit is the closure of y, and since each T_{E'} meets Z_{E'} the limit meets Z, so y is not closed; hence every closed point lies in Z.

Parts (3) and (5) (proof lines 884-899): if y in X_w specializes to z and z' in Z with distinct images x, x' in X, choose f in A with x in D(f) and x' in V(f); then in the decomposition of X_E for E = {f} the two points fall in different components, which is impossible for specializations of a common point, so x = x' and z = z', giving uniqueness of the specialization.

Part (4) (proof lines 901-908): each Z_E is a disjoint union of locally closed subschemes isomorphic to spectra of localizations of quotients of A, and a nilpotent element of such a ring pulls back to zero under some transition map, so the limit Z is reduced.
proof_roadmap: Read off ind-Zariski-ness from the construction and the bijectivity of the Z_E -> X.
Show that points outside Z fail to be closed by using the closures of their images in the partial w-localizations.
Prove uniqueness of specializations into Z by separating the images in X with a single element f.
Conclude reducedness of Z from the explicit description of the Z_E.
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects the five basic properties of the w-localization X_w of an affine scheme: A -> A_w is ind-Zariski and faithfully flat, X_w -> X is bijective on Z, Z is the set of closed points, Z is reduced, and every point of X_w specializes to a unique point of Z, so that X_w is w-local (statement lines 843-855). The proof (proof lines 857-900) derives faithful flatness from surjectivity, identifies the closed points through closures of images in the partial w-localizations, proves uniqueness of specializations by a two-point separation argument, and proves reducedness from the explicit description of Z_E. H3: five interlocking statements with an original specialization argument, all written out in full.
